title: Cartesian base change for pro-etale extension by zero with abelian coefficients
statement: Let A be a Grothendieck abelian category, in the fixed universe for sheaves on the small pro-etale sites. Let Uprime, U, Zprime and Z be schemes and let gprime : Uprime -> U, jprime : Uprime -> Zprime, j : U -> Z and g : Zprime -> Z form a cartesian square, with j and jprime open immersions. With the inverse images and extensions by zero on A-valued sheaves, the canonical map jprime_! gprime^* -> g^* j_! is an isomorphism. The canonical map is the conjugate of the weakly-etale direct-image base-change map under the two composite adjunctions. No finiteness of A or coefficients is assumed. The coefficient categories and functors are those of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero], [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction], [def-sfb-finite-upper-star].

proof.text: Restriction to an open is restriction of the small pro-etale site. In the cartesian square, the two right adjoints compute sections on canonically isomorphic fibre products: for V -> U, (V x_U Uprime) is canonically V x_Z Zprime. The identification respects restriction maps and is the weakly-etale direct-image base-change map. Thus that right-adjoint comparison is invertible.

proof.text: Compose the pullback/direct-image adjunctions with the open-extension/restriction adjunctions. Conjugation between these composite adjunctions preserves invertibility, so the canonical left-adjoint comparison is invertible. This is exactly the source-library proof of isIso_openImmersionLowerShriekBaseChangeMap, already complete before this delivery.
